title: Prisma 7.9.1 Architecture, Configuration & Migrations
outcome: Integrate Prisma 7.9.1 as a repeatable persistence layer with schema, generated client, adapter/configuration, migrations, and NestJS lifecycle.
artifact: Prisma schema + migration history + generated client + NestJS PrismaService connected to TaskFlow PostgreSQL.
labSteps: Pin Prisma packages to the course version contract and verify all Prisma package versions match.
Initialize Prisma with the intended generated-client output and PostgreSQL configuration.
Model one entity, create the first migration, and inspect the SQL before applying it.
Generate the client and wire a PrismaService into NestJS with controlled lifecycle.
Perform a smoke query through the service, then inspect the created database object independently.
Cause a safe migration/configuration failure and practice reading Prisma error codes instead of reinstalling randomly.
failureModes: Using db push as a substitute for migration history in team environments
Creating a new PrismaClient per request
mastery: Can explain schema vs migration vs generated client
Can create and inspect a migration
Can wire Prisma to NestJS cleanly
principles: Use Prisma migrations as the authoritative history of application schema changes.
Keep generated Prisma Client code derived from the schema instead of hand-editing it.
Use a shared Prisma service in NestJS so connection lifecycle and access patterns remain controlled.
Pin Prisma versions deliberately when the course architecture depends on a specific configuration model.
